data.narrative:
eleQtron, a Series A quantum computing company founded by Christof Wunderlich, Michael Johanning, and Jan Henrik Leisse, has raised €50M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comparables (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $50M as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within quantum computing; while 6 same-sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints in filtered cohorts, making sector-wide medians unreliably broad.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M–$115M, with a median point of $100M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly-filtered stage and valuation-tier peers in quantum computing, making it difficult to benchmark against direct comparables, and the typical execution risk inherent in early-stage deep tech capital intensity and commercialization timelines.
